spcpt_2vvNnwbNvPQxHkr4.name: Differences in orbits
spcpt_2vvNnwbNvPQxHkr4.definition: describe the differences in the orbits of comets, moons and planets

spcpt_3fgnr6zDGRbcpw96.name: The Doppler effect
spcpt_3fgnr6zDGRbcpw96.definition: explain why there is a change in the observed frequency and wavelength of a wave when its source is moving relative to an observer, and that this is known as the Doppler effect

spcpt_483tNYgS2GX5pBCD.name: Dangers of radiation
spcpt_483tNYgS2GX5pBCD.definition:
describe the dangers of ionising radiations, including: 
• that radiation can cause mutations in living organisms
• that radiation can damage cells and tissue
• the problems arising from the disposal of radioactive waste and how the associated risks can be reduced.

spcpt_5XHYjtMhbvX2ktKd.name: Electromagnetism

spcpt_5n5hj4GytSQNvRXC.name: Fusion
spcpt_5n5hj4GytSQNvRXC.definition: describe nuclear fusion as the creation of larger nuclei resulting in a loss of mass from smaller nuclei, accompanied by a release of energy

spcpt_62KcVXsrvdp7HsyB.name: Core practical 4: investigating refraction

spcpt_8QsrYMysQ3wvBV8N.name: The conditions for fusion
spcpt_8QsrYMysQ3wvBV8N.definition: explain why nuclear fusion does not happen at low temperatures and pressures, due to electrostatic repulsion of protons

spcpt_DMBbFvJzKPPm6WcB.definition: explain that all waves can be reflected and refracted

use the relationship between the pressure and volume of a fixed mass of gas at constant temperature: 
p1 V1 = p2 V2

spcpt_F47Gfd3vKxPHSh8K.definition: know that photographic film or a Geiger−Müller detector can detect ionising radiations

spcpt_FtK5s898xkbYMc2z.name: Frequency & time period
spcpt_FtK5s898xkbYMc2z.definition:
use the relationship between frequency and time period: frequency = 1 / time period 
f = 1 / T

spcpt_GRrqM2RpTh3wgGVN.name: Calculating half-life
spcpt_GRrqM2RpTh3wgGVN.definition: use the concept of the half-life to carry out simple calculations on activity, including graphical methods

spcpt_HRk2sv9jmG8TKPzx.name: The law of reflection
spcpt_HRk2sv9jmG8TKPzx.definition: use the law of reflection (the angle of incidence equals the angle of reflection)

spcpt_Hvfv2rqRPsQj6Tth.definition: know that fusion is the energy source for stars

spcpt_KGmkpjKQgVYDgtcJ.definition: describe the properties of magnetically hard and soft materials

spcpt_KbXCXQZpNxjQDY8J.definition: know that light waves are transverse waves and that they can be reflected and refracted

know and use the relationship between critical angle and refractive index: 
sin c = 1 / n

spcpt_T6kSK6gX9S4Yh66t.definition:
know and use the relationship between the speed, frequency and wavelength of a wave: 
wave speed = frequency × wavelength 
v = f × λ

explain some of the uses of electromagnetic radiations, including: 
• radio waves: broadcasting and communications
• microwaves: cooking and satellite transmissions
• infrared: heaters and night vision equipment
• visible light: optical fibres and photography
• ultraviolet: fluorescent lamps
• x-rays: observing the internal structure of objects and materials, including for medical applications
• gamma rays: sterilising food and medical equipment.

spcpt_ZXdQ84K5D77zz99c.name: Waves & energy
spcpt_ZXdQ84K5D77zz99c.definition: know that waves transfer energy and information without transferring matter

spcpt_ZYrty2Br6r3hRWgs.name: Chain reactions

spcpt_bJNjcGSCgwkPd7Yb.name: Orbital motion
spcpt_bJNjcGSCgwkPd7Yb.definition:
explain that gravitational force: 
• causes moons to orbit planets
• causes the planets to orbit the Sun
• causes artificial satellites to orbit the Earth
• causes comets to orbit the Sun.

spcpt_brbbw8yJH45q2WpC.name: Total internal reflection

spcpt_cFwJhrmB466WjKy5.definition: know that a voltage is induced in a conductor or a coil when it moves through a magnetic field or when a magnetic field changes through it and describe the factors that affect the size of the induced voltage

spcpt_cmpPWCPgPTS4FmvD.definition:
describe the evolution of stars of similar mass to the Sun through the following stages: 
• nebula
• star (main sequence)
• red giant
• white dwarf.

spcpt_csCqV6JfsMWkwFhd.name: Sound
spcpt_csCqV6JfsMWkwFhd.definition: know that sound waves are longitudinal waves which can be reflected and refracted

spcpt_czwXCx8YcQDbBMrj.name: Critical angle

spcpt_dBhXphBvfbYPqbJJ.name: Half life

spcpt_f77qyH7vc8Tk7qWF.definition: know that magnets repel and attract other magnets and attract magnetic substances

spcpt_fNQmdwQyt6x866bb.definition: describe the effects on the atomic and mass numbers of a nucleus of the emission of each of the four main types of radiation (alpha, beta, gamma and neutron radiation)

spcpt_h8jSXWBHj8tmp3J5.name: Calculations in different contexts
spcpt_h8jSXWBHj8tmp3J5.definition: use the above relationships in different contexts including sound waves and electromagnetic waves

spcpt_hQKxDSVhJF3GgDCb.definition: describe the nature of alpha (α) particles, beta (β−) particles, and gamma (γ) rays, and recall that they may be distinguished in terms of penetrating power and ability to ionise

spcpt_hgmkjchdVz77kH85.definition: describe how the force on a current-carrying conductor in a magnetic field changes with the magnitude and direction of the field and current

spcpt_kM5HsJQ4XMc9sN7k.definition: Core practical 13: investigate the penetration powers of different types of radiation using either radioactive sources or simulations

spcpt_kTccWnDYYcz48mPY.definition:
use the relationship between orbital speed, orbital radius and time period: 
orbital speed = 2 x π x orbital radius / time period
v = 2 x π × r / T

spcpt_kfxX5zrCqRCp7f2W.name: The gas laws
spcpt_kfxX5zrCqRCp7f2W.definition:
explain, for a fixed amount of gas, the qualitative relationship between: 
• pressure and volume at constant temperature
• pressure and Kelvin temperature at constant volume.

spcpt_kn9T8XCzVhpC5tb8.definition:
explain the detrimental effects of excessive exposure of the human body to electromagnetic waves, including: 
• microwaves: internal heating of body tissue
• infrared: skin burns
• ultraviolet: damage to surface cells and blindness
• gamma rays: cancer, mutation
and describe simple protective measures against the risks

spcpt_kzfGQ76PPCcH8cC7.definition: describe the evolution of stars with a mass larger than the Sun

spcpt_m7zPrD837GFQJp78.definition:
know that: 
• the universe is a large collection of billions of galaxies
• a galaxy is a large collection of billions of stars
• our solar system is in the Milky Way galaxy.

spcpt_mhY7msFPwnFBHT53.name: Ray diagrams
spcpt_mhY7msFPwnFBHT53.definition: draw ray diagrams to illustrate reflection and refraction

spcpt_mjF6GS3g92TS38PH.name: Gravitational field strength
spcpt_mjF6GS3g92TS38PH.definition: understand why gravitational field strength, g, varies and know that it is different on other planets and the Moon from that on the Earth

spcpt_mkDnwkbVvY23ND8y.definition:
know and use the relationship between refractive index, angle of incidence and angle of refraction: 
n = sin i / sin r

spcpt_nQP3FR7WskG2YhJt.name: Uses of radioactivity
spcpt_nQP3FR7WskG2YhJt.definition: describe uses of radioactivity in industry and medicine

spcpt_nvZs6Z2NqZBSPj3j.name: Transverse & longitudinal waves
spcpt_nvZs6Z2NqZBSPj3j.definition: explain the difference between longitudinal and transverse waves

spcpt_qK87nMmfSTSdX7H5.name: Absolute zero
spcpt_qK87nMmfSTSdX7H5.definition: understand why there is an absolute zero of temperature which is –273 °C

spcpt_qkgDJsZQDJG7Vy5b.definition: describe the structure of an atom in terms of protons, neutrons and electrons and use symbols such as 14/6 c to describe particular nuclei

spcpt_qwrQbzyxGk5BhDwF.name: Permanent & induced magnets
spcpt_qwrQbzyxGk5BhDwF.definition: know that magnetism is induced in some materials when they are placed in a magnetic field

spcpt_rNHHCKfdcPPf3sYJ.definition: describe the difference between contamination and irradiation
